The exam cannot catch this because it exercises the happy path and the tag-absent path only. The design rule the task states is "attribution is best-effort, never a park" for *frontier* facts; a missing compiler is not one. fleet/launch.mjs: after `git fetch origin <default>` the launcher force-writes `refs/remotes/origin/<default>` to `origin.tip` — the sha read by the *earlier* `ls-remote`. If the origin's default branch advances between the `ls-remote` and the `fetch`, the fetch brings the newer tip and this `update-ref` then moves the operator's tracking ref *backwards* to the stale sha, with no old-value guard and no reflog message. M3 still passes (one ref changed), so this is advisory. Cheapest fix that keeps the exec-log pin `fetch origin main` intact: pass the expected old value — `['update-ref', ref, origin.tip, <sha the ref held before the fetch>]` is not available, so instead only write the ref when it is absent, e.g. read `git rev-parse --verify --quiet refs/remotes/origin/<b>` after the fetch and `update-ref` only when that read answers non-zero (the case the comment actually describes: a fetch whose refspec did not cover the branch). Add `-m 'launch: default-branch read'` while there.; fleet/launch.mjs: the shallow gate only fires on `shallow.code === 0 && stdout === 'true'`; a `rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` that answers non-zero (a git too old to know the flag, or any other failure) falls through silently. A shallow clone that slips past it then fails at `merge-base --is-ancestor` and is refused with BASE_OFF_MAIN_FIX — 'relaunch from main' — which is the wrong instruction for a truncated history and sends the operator to re-drive work that was never parked. M2 is unaffected (the exam's clone answers `true`), so this is advisory. Suggest either refusing on a non-zero `--is-shallow-repository` read as its own unreadable-checkout Refusal, or falling back to `test -f $(git rev-parse --git-dir)/shallow` before proceeding.

Read together, the nearest antecedent of "It" is the fold unit / `fleet/publish-fold.mjs`, but `push_head` is the boot script's shell function: this plan's sibling tasks state that the folder "pushes nothing, opens nothing and writes no status page" (task 3's Context) and that `push_head` runs in `do_boot`'s bracket after `await_engine_inactive fleet-fold-<N>-2` (task 4). The contract is the authority for these literals, so the ambiguity should be removed. Nothing in the Proof exercises this sentence (all Run pins are green), hence minor, and the later "after the engine" line — "the head is on the remote (`push_head`'s `git push origin ultra/integration-run-N`)" — already places the push correctly in the boot script's sequence.; unverified: the contract now pins literals that live in sibling-owned files — the fold unit's full `systemd-run` argv (`fleet-fold-<N>-<attempt>`, `<engine>/fleet/publish-fold.mjs --repo … --attempt 1|2`), the merge-retry order (`running "publish fold (attempt 2)"` → re-fold → lease push → `publishing` → re-entered check-runs loop → one further PUT), the six dispositions and the `publish-fold/receipt.json` shape. What would settle it: task 4's merge/boot sims run on the adopted tree, where those three CONTRACT.md cases read the edited contract against the sibling's boot script. task 3: exam: fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs:648 cannot pass under any implementation, and it is why the run exits 1. It reads `git rev-parse <TIP>^{tree}` in the target clone as the FIRST statement of leg (d) — before `publishFold` is called, so no code of mine has run. That clone was cut from the origin before main moved; `mainCommit`/`pushMain` make the commit in the second clone and push it to the origin, and nothing between there and line 648 fetches into the target clone (`provision` -> `provisionRunTree` -> `cloneAtBase` only clones OUT of it, run-waves.mjs:61-87, `--local`, never a fetch). Git says so itself: `fatal: ambiguous argument '<tip>^{tree}': unknown revision or path not in the working tree`. The same read at line 696 is fine, because by then the folder has fetched TIP into the clone. The leg's intent (`fixture sanity: TIP did not move`) is preserved by taking both reads from `fx.maker`, which holds the object throughout; that is the one-word change I made in the scratch copy and did not make in the tree.

completenessFindings.detail: Task 3's deliverable `fleet/publish-fold.mjs` is absent from the integrated tree (only `fleet/publish-fold-block.mjs` and `fleet/tests/test_publish_fold_block.mjs` exist; there is no `fleet/tests/test_publish_fold.mjs`), yet Task 4's `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` landed its caller unconditionally. `do_boot` runs `publish_fold 1` at fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:1645 for every outcome with commits ahead of BASE, and `publish_fold` at fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:925-935 launches `node "$ENGINE_REPO_DIR/fleet/publish-fold.mjs"`. With that file missing, node exits non-zero, `fold_field <attempt> disposition` is empty, so the crash branch at fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:960-971 writes `disposition "cannot fold"`, `fold_hold_note` (fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:897-905) sets `FOLD_HOLD="left open: publish fold — cannot fold: exit …"`, and `merge_pr` (fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:1336-1338) then reads no check runs and issues no PUT. The integrated tree therefore not only fails the plan's own Claim ('two plans that touch the same file … both merge on their own — no 405, no hand rebase — and the second one's evidence shows the fold it did onto main') and Task 3's Claim ('the sandbox folds its own integration branch onto main's tip at publish'), it regresses the pre-existing green path: every gate-green run that previously self-merged is now held open at `cannot fold`. This is invisible to the per-task referees because Task 4's sim stubs the `fleet-fold-*` unit through `systemd-run` and never executes the script. Task 2's `contendingBlock` export in fleet/publish-fold-block.mjs and Task 1's `resolveConflicts` export in fleet/run-engine.mjs:567 are correspondingly unreferenced by any production caller — the only consumer named in the dependency edges (1 -> 3, 2 -> 3) did not land.

Context literal disagreement between Task 6 (`fleet/CONTRACT.md`) and the tree: the contract, which is the stated authority for every fleet literal, documents machinery that is not present. fleet/CONTRACT.md:158-168 names `<engine>/fleet/publish-fold.mjs` as what the `fleet-fold-<N>-<attempt>` unit runs, and fleet/CONTRACT.md:48-52 describes the `publish-fold/receipt.json` shape and the `engine-head`, `main.patch`, `run.patch`, `frontier/wave-<attempt>/`, `resolver-brief-<i>-<attempt>.txt`, `suite-<attempt>.txt` receipts as things that file writes — none of which any code in the tree produces. Task 6's own Claim and Proof are met by the document in isolation (its Run: pins all pass, and the receipt shape, disposition vocabulary `folded`/`nothing to join`/`tip unmoved`/`suite red`/`conflict parked`/`cannot fold`, the `Fleet-Run: <N>` / `Plan-Tag: ultra/plan/run-<N>` trailers and the `left open: merge PUT answered 405 twice` note all agree byte-for-byte with fleet/sandbox-boot.sh:824-905, 1406-1408 and 1686), so this is a document-ahead-of-tree divergence that resolves the moment Task 3 lands rather than an independent defect.
